A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the polytropic index, and hence the equation of state of the gas, is determined by the balance of the various heating and cooling mechanisms in a gas cloud.

the equation of state of interstellar gas is highly non-isothermal, with the adiabat varying between 0.1-1.5, and that it is strongly affected by the velocity field and the metallicity of the interstellar medium.

The main takeaway from our work is that

the equation of state of interstellar gas clouds, and hence the stellar initial mass function, is highly sensitive to the metallicity and radiation field, and that the adiabat is generally not close to unity.
the equation of state of interstellar gas clouds is not a universal property of the ISM.
the equation of state of the interstellar medium is highly non-adiabatic, and this has important consequences for the formation of massive stars.
